reading.body:
ELEVATE Government Affairs filed 130 AI lobbying reports, and its biggest AI client is Microsoft, with 15 filings.

The client list splits into two groups. Microsoft, Meta, and Applied Digital are technology and data center companies. Five players associations, covering basketball, football, baseball, soccer, and hockey, account for 71 of the filings between them. A single firm carrying both the largest AI platform companies and the major sports unions suggests AI policy work now reaches well beyond the technology sector.

The lobbyist counts show how the work is staffed. Robert Chamberlin appears on 125 of the firm's AI filings and Samuel Whitehorn on 123, so two people carry nearly the whole AI portfolio. The remaining eight named lobbyists range from 95 filings down to 2.

The data covers filings only. It records that a client was named on a report about AI, not what position the firm argued, and it does not show spending amounts, which bills were targeted, or outcomes. Nothing here ties this lobbying to compute, buildings, or power directly, though the presence of Microsoft, Meta, and Applied Digital among the clients is consistent with AI policy work that touches data center and infrastructure questions.

summary: ELEVATE GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS, LLC filed 130 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 401105417.
